# foundry_file (Resource)

Uploads a file for use by other Foundry resources. Files are immutable, so any change forces a new file to be uploaded.

Use this resource when the file is part of what Terraform manages, such as a document attached to a vector store an agent then searches. If the file is instead loaded once, or published by a separate data pipeline, upload it there and use the `foundry_files` data source to look up its ID: files are identified by a service-assigned ID rather than by name, so a lookup is the only way to reference a file this configuration did not create.

The file contents are read and uploaded during `terraform apply`, so apply time grows with file size.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "foundry_file" "manual" {
  source_path = "${path.module}/manual.pdf"
  purpose     = "assistants"
  source_hash = filesha256("${path.module}/manual.pdf")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `purpose` (String) Intended purpose of the file, such as `assistants`, `batch`, `fine-tune`, `evals`, `vision`, or `user_data`. The accepted set varies by service version. Required when uploading a file; the service reports it back, so an imported file does not need it in the configuration.
- `source_hash` (String) Hash of the file contents, such as `filesha256("path")`. Supply this to force a re-upload when the file contents change.
- `source_path` (String) Local path of the file to upload. Required when uploading a file; it is optional only so that an imported file, whose local path the service cannot report, does not plan a replacement.

### Read-Only

- `bytes` (Number) Size of the uploaded file in bytes.
- `created_at` (Number) Unix timestamp when the file was uploaded.
- `filename` (String) Name the service recorded for the uploaded file.
- `id` (String) Service-assigned file identifier.
- `status` (String) Processing status of the uploaded file.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Files are imported using the file ID.
terraform import foundry_file.manual assistant-65DSKHVDB1VPFg4jdJc84h
```
